headline: Highest risk is medium: shared-network pair has no documented shared workspace, but opik can egress broadly while risingwave is network-restricted, creating limited leakage and coordination risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. opik only shows REST API egress, while risingwave shows no I/O surfaces or shared filesystem/MCP bridge. Without a bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, reassess upward.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's raw outputs as instructions, prompt-injection risk appears.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Do not pipe one agent's raw output into the other's prompt.
Add provenance tags if a bridge is introduced.
requires-engineering: enforce channel-level allowlists for any future integration.

B_data_leakage.rationale: opik has broad network egress, but the profiles show no data classes touched and risingwave has no documented sensitive-data handling or shared workspace. Leakage is therefore not evidenced in default use, though any shared workspace plus opik's egress would raise exposure.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF opik is configured to transmit file contents or prompts externally, data exposure becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Run opik on non-sensitive test data only.
Disable outbound access where possible.
Review any REST API destinations before use.
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation or per-agent mounts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented. opik exposes REST API egress only, and risingwave has no listed write targets, OAuth scopes, or filesystem surfaces. With no shared mutable resource, capability conflict is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or database, conflict risk appears.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locks or mutable state, reassess for contention.
mitigations: Avoid giving both agents write access to the same resource.
Separate credentials per agent.
Keep git/database state outside the pair.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable store.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pipeline where risingwave consumes opik outputs as authoritative input. opik can emit via REST API, but risingwave's profile shows no downstream action-taking authority or input parser, so cascading error is only a weak possibility if an operator manually chains them.
conditions: IF opik outputs are manually copied into risingwave jobs without verification, cascading errors become plausible.
IF risingwave is configured to act on opik-generated facts automatically, severity increases.
mitigations: Verify any opik output before reuse.
Do not automate action-taking from unreviewed summaries.
Use a human review step between agents.
requires-engineering: add schema validation on handoff payloads.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. opik and risingwave are both open-source with empty data-class fields, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to score.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced, reassess compliance obligations.
IF either project is deployed under a residency or retention policy not shown here, the profile is incomplete.
mitigations: Confirm the data classes before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of the pair until policies are reviewed.
Document retention and residency settings.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
